findings.title: transform_messages / normalize_tool_pairs is dead wire
findings.description: Public functions documented as 'single wire choke-point' for ToolCall/ToolResult pairing repair have zero production callers. Compaction/truncation/interrupted turns ship un-repaired history to providers, causing 400s on Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini.
findings.fix: Insert normalize_tool_pairs into HttpProvider::execute_once as the actual wire choke-point, OR delete the functions and rewrite their docs to say 'pairing is caller's responsibility'.

findings.title: Dreaming stages never call push_pending; queue is ingest-only
findings.description: embedding_manager.rs:25 docstring claims 'Producers (ingest tail, dream stage tails) are wired in B5.2' but only the ingest tail (notes/ingest/ingestor/batch.rs:230-241) calls push_pending/flush_pending. 10+ dream stages (note_decay, note_consolidate, note_synthesis, note_lint, note_review, mention_weave, note_weave, goal_lessons_promote, dreaming/mod.rs:2498) all write notes and bypass the queue, leaving vectors stale until manual reembed_all RPC.
findings.fix: Either wire a background flusher task (as the docstring promises) and have every stage tail push_pending, or remove the queue and re-embed on the read path.

findings.title: push_staged uses non-atomic tokio::fs::write where atomic_write_file is expected
findings.description: apply transaction's whole point is stage-then-rename atomically; push_staged writes the staged file with plain tokio::fs::write (not atomic_write_file as every other note writer does). A crash mid-write leaves a half-written staged .md file that gets renamed to the target, shipping a corrupt markdown blob as the new source-of-truth note.
findings.fix: Replace tokio::fs::write(&staged_path, &body) with atomic_write_file(&staged_path, &body).

findings.title: commit reports linked and pushes touched_paths for every PageOp::Link regardless of add_link success
findings.description: Two issues: (1) add_link(from, to) returns Ok(()) on a split_path failure (silently skipped), but commit's report.linked += 1 and touched_paths.push() fire unconditionally. (2) The second add_link(to, from) call relies on the implementation's inverted argument order — add_link treats its first arg as the note-to-append-to — so the bidirectional intent works today but a refactor renaming the parameter would silently break it.
findings.fix: Track per-direction success/failure and skip the report increment on failure. Rename the function argument to make the bidirectional logic self-documenting.

findings.title: embedding-queue path uses lossy replace('..', '') contrary to recent 'reject titles containing ..' policy
findings.description: ingest_batch computes safe_path = path.replace('..', '').replace('\\', '/') for the post-commit embedding-queue push — the exact lossy pattern 2b1813429 removed from note/helpers.rs. Defensive in current call graph (paths come from report.touched_paths post-sanitize), but masks any future regression where a caller bypasses sanitize_title.
findings.fix: Replace with sanitize_title or the note_content_path helper. If defensive-only is intentional, add a 'should never trigger' assertion.

findings.title: <memory> fence from render_markdown_v1 not in DISCARD_TAG_PAIRS
findings.description: MessageAssembler builds its scrubber with DISCARD_TAG_PAIRS, which excludes the <memory>...</memory> outer fence and the six inner slot fences (<user_profile>, <session_recent>, etc.) that the production MarkdownV1 render style emits. If the LLM echoes the framing back, the terminal sanitize path also lacks coverage, so raw <memory>...</memory> tags reach the user.
findings.fix: Add MarkdownV1 fences to DISCARD_TAG_PAIRS (or have the scrubber read RenderStyle at construction time) and extend OTHER_STRIP_TAGS in sanitize.rs to match. Extend the discard_tag_pairs_*_matches_canonical_fence drift-guard test to cover all the fences.

findings.title: UnknownFlow after successful routing leaves no graceful fallback
findings.description: Step 1 has a graceful fallback ONLY for UnknownAgent (resolves to default-agent, overrides spec.agent). UnknownFlow returns hard error. The default_routing table maps every builtin SubAgent id to a same-named flow id, but loop-auditor has no matching preset. Latent today (gateway sends agent_id='main'), but a 1-line change makes it user-visible.

findings.title: SessionStrategy::Child resolves parent but never persists it
findings.description: resolve_session computes SessionResolution.parent_session_key for Child strategy, but Orchestrator::dispatch only reads session_key. parent_session_key is discarded. The session is created in the store without ever setting the column, even though schema/query handlers all read it.

findings.title: PiiEngine::reload lacks the partial-load summary warning emitted by new
findings.description: PiiEngine::new computes configured_custom - loaded_custom and emits one operator-facing warn! summarising partial custom-rule load. PiiEngine::reload does not — it calls the same build_rules but skips the summary. Hot-reload of a half-broken config yields per-rule warns but no top-level signal. Asymmetric operational story between boot and reload.
findings.fix: Reuse the same configured_custom / loaded_custom logic in reload (extract into a helper), or drop it from both.

findings.title: Provider-tier PII filter ignores platform-aware exclusion
findings.description: HttpProvider::apply_outbound_safety gates the per-text-block PII filter on is_provider_excluded (global) only and calls engine.filter() (also global, no platform). It does NOT consult is_platform_excluded nor receive a platform name. Operators with [platform_policies.X].exclude_providers bypassed at runtime_guard are surprised at http_provider re-applying PII filtering on the unredacted payload. Same gap also downgrades per-platform PII action overrides (e.g. platform_policies.X.phone = warn).
findings.fix: Propagate platform name through execute/apply_outbound_safety and call is_platform_excluded(platform, provider) + filter_with_platform; OR remove the second-tier PII filter from apply_outbound_safety on the grounds that the guardrail pipeline already covers it.

findings.title: CodexAuth::ensure_valid is dead code
findings.description: ensure_valid has zero callers across the codebase. Real refresh path goes through gateway/codex_token_refresher.rs and gateway/handlers/oauth.rs::try_refresh, which directly call CodexAuth::refresh().
findings.fix: Delete ensure_valid, or route one of the two real call sites through it to remove the duplicate refresh+swap pattern.

findings.title: Entire agent_events Skeleton & Pulse surface unused (9 methods + 7 TYPE_* constants)
findings.description: All 9 CRUD methods on agent_events (insert_event, bulk_insert_events, get_events_by_task, get_events_since_seq, get_events_in_range, get_structural_events, get_latest_event_seq, delete_events_for_task, get_event_count) have zero production callers. AgentEvent TYPE_* constants likewise unused.

findings.title: experience_replays migration is dead (no Cortex consumer)
findings.description: migrate_add_experience_replays creates experience_replays + 4 indexes + experiences_vec vec0; nothing reads or writes them anywhere in the tree.

findings.title: MemoryStats struct fully orphaned (re-exported from 3 sites, no consumers)
findings.description: Defined in state_database/mod.rs and re-exported from database::mod.rs, resilience::mod.rs, and lib.rs:220. Webchat has its own unrelated MemoryStats. No production reader.

findings.title: POE tables (poe_events / poe_trust_scores / poe_contracts) fully orphaned
findings.description: Three POE tables with 5 indexes are created on every StateDatabase::new() but no production code reads or writes them. Pure dead schema.

findings.title: Inert retention_cap knob (form-3)
findings.description: RoutingExperienceStore.retention_cap is hardcoded to DEFAULT_ROUTING_RETENTION_CAP=5000 with no setter or constructor parameter; form-3 severed wire.

findings.title: Empty api_key treated as Available
findings.description: provider_availability_from_config treats Some("") empty api_key as ProviderStatus::Available, falsely tagging misconfigured providers and recommending them in the recall block.

findings.title: Empty agent_id in binding silently routes to default agent
findings.description: When a binding's agent_id is empty, resolve_route routes to DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=main instead of falling through to the unmatched default-path. Indistinguishable from a deliberate 'main' match.

findings.title: call_api has no retry, no backoff, no Retry-After parsing
findings.description: A single HTTP request. Any non-2xx response or network error becomes AlephError::config that flush_pending catches and drops the batch. No retry, no exponential backoff, no circuit breaker. A single 503 from the remote provider drops an entire ingest batch's embeddings. Combined with F-02, transient errors on the dream-tail path mean vectors stay absent permanently.
findings.fix: Wrap request.send() in a small retry loop with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. Distinguish transient (5xx, network) from configuration (4xx) errors so flush_pending can push transient-failed items back to the queue front rather than drop them.

findings.title: Embedding signature uses config id, not preset
findings.description: format!('{provider_id}:{model_name}:{dim}') uses the user's config id, but two different ids (e.g. openai-prod, openai-dev) on the same preset produce different signatures, forcing a full reembed when the actual weights are unchanged. Conversely, two providers with the same id (from different machines) write the same signature even if they point at different weights.
findings.fix: Sign the preset as well: format!('{preset}:{p}:{m}:{d}'). One extra lookup at record time, avoids unnecessary reembeds on operator rename.

findings.title: EnvelopeRelevanceFloorExtension registered with floor=0.0 (no-op)
findings.description: agent_init/mod.rs:319-322 registers the extension with new(0.0). The comment at 317-318 says 'no-op at floor=0.0 to prove end-to-end plumbing. Real floor could be plumbed from config later.' The registration consumes a slot in the registry and the per-call extension-chain walk adds latency for zero observable behaviour.
findings.fix: Either plumb the floor from [memory.orientation]/[memory.extensions] envelope_floor config, or gate the registration behind 'if cfg.envelope_floor > 0.0' so the empty chain is only assembled when there is something to do. Per R10 YAGNI, prefer the gate.

findings.title: aggregate_tool_usage and aggregate_tool_failures may double-read ToolInvocation rows
findings.description: Tool-signal-sink module doc identifies exactly two readers of RawMemorySource::ToolInvocation: aggregate_tool_usage (admin RPC) and aggregate_tool_failures (tool_failure_distill dream stage). If one consumer marks rows processed and the other then sees an empty set, the failure distiller silently stops seeing failures.
findings.fix: Audit whether mark_raw_as_processed covers ToolInvocation rows on both paths. Add a per-consumer cursor if it does, or a processed_by watermark.

findings.title: reconcile_corpus prune loop falls back to 'other' on sanitize_title failure, can drop valid index rows
findings.description: The loop checks CATEGORY_DIRS.contains(&entry.category.as_str()) first, then sanitize_title(category). If the row's category is one of the 21 valid CATEGORY_DIRS values, sanitize is idempotent and works. If it's a legacy unsafe value (rows from pre-policy DB), the fallback 'other' is used for the file lookup, the file is not found, and the row is removed from the index while its on-disk file survives. Recoverable only on a full_rebuild_all over every corpus.
findings.fix: Use entry.category directly (the guard already constrains the value to CATEGORY_DIRS), or log a tracing::warn! on the sanitize failure instead of falling through.

findings.title: add_link silently skips on split_path failure or missing file; caller still increments linked
findings.description: split_path failure returns Ok(()) with no side effect; try_exists == false returns Ok(()) too. The commit loop increments report.linked += 1 unconditionally. A malformed PageOp::Link is indistinguishable from a successful link in the apply report and CompressionService's downstream accounting.
findings.fix: Track skipped-link reasons and surface them in the report. The commit site should not increment linked unless both directions verified.

findings.title: mark_superseded re-reads file from disk after the vault watcher may have indexed it (TOCTOU of intent, not data)
findings.description: mark_superseded reads body, appends a marker, atomic_write_file, then re-parses in-memory (not a disk read) and index_notes. The vault watcher may concurrently index the new bytes; both calls go through SQLite's mutex serially, so the final state is consistent. The visible artifact is a spurious 're-indexed externally edited note' watcher log for what was a self-write.
findings.fix: Add a code comment documenting the expected double-index on self-supersedes.

findings.title: dedup_redirect_creates silently drops Create.relations on merge
findings.description: When a Create is merged into an Append against an existing note, the rewrite hardcodes new_relations: vec![], dropping the typed entity-graph frontmatter relations. The dedup is logged but the missing edge is invisible downstream.
findings.fix: Carry relations through as new_relations: relations.clone() in the destructure; index_note's upsert path already dedupes by (from, to_note) so duplicates are safe.

findings.title: note_type_as_str_values_are_unique misses 4 of 15 variants
findings.description: arb_note_type generates 15 variants (Lesson, Skill, Reference, Transcript added after Preference, Plan, ...). The deterministic note_type_as_str_values_are_unique test lists only 11. The proptest covers all 15 today, but a future contributor adding a variant who only updates arb_note_type will silently leave the deterministic test out of date.
findings.fix: Replace the hand-listed all_variants with a const fn enumerating the enum (or derive strum::EnumIter), or guard with 'assert_eq!(all_variants.len(), 15)' so a missing entry is a loud failure.

findings.title: Three extract_depth copies with different first/last /d semantics
findings.description: mod.rs:137 (split('/d').nth(1) — first), summary_source.rs:135 (split('/').find_map strip_prefix('d') — first d-segment), session_search_summary/end_hook.rs:34 (rfind('/d') — last) all parse aleph://session/{sid}/d{depth}/{seq} but give different answers when session_id contains '/d'. The end_hook copy is the only one with a documented correct invariant.
findings.fix: Promote the end_hook.rs:34 version to session_compactor::extract_depth and delete both copies.

findings.title: prune_orphan_vectors deletes vec-table rows before map rows — crash leaves ghost KNN hits
findings.description: On a crash between DELETE FROM notes_vec_<dim> and DELETE FROM notes_vec_map, the vec table has dangling rows with no map entry. KNN filtering tolerates this (the post-KNN map lookup drops the dangling rowids), but the dangling slots consume KNN capacity that no indexed note occupies. The recent aa4f63b27 fix addressed the unbounded case but not the ordering.
findings.fix: Delete from notes_vec_map first, then from vec tables, so the surviving state on crash is 'dangling vec slots' rather than 'vec slots no one can map'. Alternatively, commit both DELETE statements in a sub-transaction.

findings.title: get_embedding silently returns wrong-length Vec<f32> on blob/dim mismatch
findings.description: The decode b.chunks_exact(4).map(f32::from_le_bytes) silently drops any trailing bytes when the blob's byte length is not a multiple of dim*4. Callers (find_similar_notes) compute cosine on a partial vector with no error.
findings.fix: Validate blob.len() == dim_hint * 4 and return an explicit error; alternatively track the row's actual dim in notes_vec_map and verify before fetch.

findings.title: vector_search builds WHERE rowid IN (...) up to limit*3 — can exceed SQLite 32766 placeholders
findings.description: KNN is run with k = limit.saturating_mul(3).max(limit), and the post-KNN filter builds an IN-clause over those rowids. SQLite's default SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER is 32766; a pathological caller (limit > 10k) drives the placeholder count past that. The error surfaces as a 500.
findings.fix: Batch the rowid IN (...) clause the same way prune_orphan_vectors does (5000-row chunks) or document the cap at the API boundary.

findings.title: load_graph_snapshot issues one prepared statement per node for notes_sources (N+1)
findings.description: For each of n notes in the corpus, load_graph_snapshot runs a separate SELECT source_ref FROM notes_sources WHERE agent_id=? AND note_path=?. On a 50k-note vault this is 50k prepared compiles + 50k queries, all serialized by the connection mutex. graph_recompute runs this every dream cycle.
findings.fix: Batch the notes_sources fetch in one query, group by note_path in Rust.

findings.title: Orchestrator::reload_flows only replaces the registry; routing/sandbox are immutable
findings.description: Orchestrator exposes reload_flows(new_set) but no equivalent for routing_overrides, default_routing, sandbox_factory. default_routing built once at boot from agent_registry.list_ids() — new plugins/projects invisible to dispatch, fall through to UnknownAgent arm silently.

findings.title: Every gateway chat dispatch hits InvalidConfig for any SubAgent agent_id
findings.description: Six preset flows (explore, coder, researcher, default, plan, verify) declare SessionStrategy::Child with parent_session_key unset; FlowRequest::parent_session is None in gateway. Child strategy requires non-empty parent at runtime, so any routing resolution to these flows hard-fails. Latent today but a stale default_routing entry will hard-fail.

findings.title: FlowStreamEvent::Complete NOT emitted on error/cancel paths
findings.description: BroadcastCallback::on_complete_with_outcome is the ONLY emitter (single-source comment), called only on Ok arm. Error paths reach ? operator without emitting Complete. Gateway drain has a safety-net that builds from outcome.duration_ms=0; subscribers waiting on Complete frame hang on error paths.

findings.title: MoA one-shot pref consumed before the failure points it documents to restore on
findings.description: take_for_run is called early (~line 346); restore_one_shot only happens inside the try_build_for_run error arm. Between take and harness.run there are ~10 failure-capable steps. Any error consumes the one-shot without restoring it — the 'all paths leave no state' doc claim is false by inspection.

findings.title: Dead re-export: MAX_FLOW_DEPTH has zero non-test consumers
findings.description: pub use resolver::{RoutingOverrides, MAX_FLOW_DEPTH}; the only consumers are inside src/orchestrator/tests/. Same shape for ContextBudgetRefiner and ProviderChain — re-exported at mod.rs but every consumer imports from crate::orchestrator::deps_builder::*.

findings.title: PII allowlist has no direct unit tests
findings.description: src/pii/allowlist.rs ships with zero #[cfg(test)] mod tests. All coverage reaches is_allowed indirectly via engine integration tests. The static sets (TEST_PHONES, LOCAL_IPS) and the regexes (SYSTEM_EMAIL_PATTERNS — pattern widened previously by 56a84247e/c59090033 for the case-fold in both directions) are exactly where a regression in pattern semantics would land first.
findings.fix: Add a #[cfg(test)] mod with positive tests for each rule-name branch (phone, email, ip_address), a negative test for an unrelated rule (api_key returns false for everything), and a case-fold test for the email branch covering .example, .EXAMPLE, noreply@, NO-REPLY@.

findings.title: Double PII filter with divergent semantics (filter_with_platform vs filter)
findings.description: runtime_guard::process_outbound calls filter_with_platform (platform-aware); the request then continues to HttpProvider::apply_outbound_safety which calls engine.filter (global-config, no platform). The two paths use different filter functions whose semantics diverge whenever [platform_policies.X] overrides the global config. When runtime_guard elects to redact, http_provider tier is a no-op. When runtime_guard elects to skip (platform exclusion), http_provider tier may still redact. Same root cause as PII-001 framed as duplication.
findings.fix: Drop the PII block from apply_outbound_safety on the grounds that the guardrail layer already covers it; OR propagate platform name to apply_outbound_safety and gate on is_platform_excluded(None, &self.name) so the second tier does not contradict the first.

findings.title: dedup_overlapping is O(n²)
findings.description: dedup_overlapping uses result.iter().any(|existing| m.start < existing.end && m.end > existing.start) inside a loop over the input. For typical outbound PII (1–3 matches per message) this is invisible, but the path is on the hot outbound pipeline and the surrounding filter_with_config is invoked once per outbound text block. A pathological case — a long string with many adjacent rule hits, e.g. a 1-MB CSV column with many credit-card Luhn-valid numbers — would walk Vec<PiiMatch> quadratically.
findings.fix: Sort spans by (start, -end) first and run a sweep, or bucket by start/16 and check only the small bucket — either removes the quadratic worst-case while preserving semantics.

findings.title: FilterResult.skipped_count is computed but never read
findings.description: skipped_count is set in filter_with_config whenever a Block action cannot be applied because matched offsets fall off a char boundary / outside the (mutated) text. The doc-comment explicitly says the audit pipeline (runtime_guard) can use this as a triage signal. Grep across src/ and tests/ finds zero non-test readers — runtime_guard::apply_filter_result only reads blocked_count and warned_count. The field is permanently zero-valued for any consumer.
findings.fix: Either wire apply_filter_result to escalate skipped_count > 0 to a Critical audit entry (the original intent) and document the convention, or drop the field.

findings.title: is_oauth_token sniff doesn't account for base_url
findings.description: Decision is key-prefix-only (sk-ant-, eyJ, cc-). If OAuth token is paired with non-official base_url (Bedrock/Vertex), Claude Code identity + OAuth betas are still injected → 400 from third-party. Conversely Bedrock/Vertex may use IAM tokens that don't match sk-ant-* prefix.
findings.fix: Combine (key_prefix, base_url) decision: force is_oauth=false when base_url hits Bedrock/Vertex/Azure, warn when official endpoint meets non-sk-ant key.

findings.title: llm_retry::backoff_delay is dead code
findings.description: backoff_delay is documented as the unified exponential growth helper and referenced from failover/mod.rs:80 + failover/provider.rs:1285, but has zero callers. failover has its own local implementation (gateway/delivery_queue.rs::backoff_delay).
findings.fix: Either have failover/provider.rs really call llm_retry::backoff_delay to honor the docs, or delete the function and update the docs to admit failover has its own backoff.

findings.title: ProviderPreset::description length not constrained vs ProviderMetadata::notes 'under ~80 chars' contract
findings.description: metadata.rs:79 documents notes as 'kept under ~80 chars'. PRESET_METADATA lazy init (line 1018-1027) blindly assigns preset.description to notes with no length gate. No current string violates, but no compile-time or runtime barrier prevents future PRs from violating.
findings.fix: Add assert!(desc.len() <= 80) in with_description ctor or at the lazy-init site.

findings.title: Anthropic ThinkingSignatureDelta accumulation relies on byte-order assumption
findings.description: Signature fragments are concatenated via simple +=. Works for current Anthropic 4.5+ stream format (multiple signature_delta events) but breaks if delivery moves to base64 chunks, multi-signature rotation, or signature-in-content_block_stop.
findings.fix: Probe stream format and key concatenation on event_type not on byte order. Add a fallback for signature-only-final delivery.

findings.title: Gemini SSE adapter lacks truncation guard
findings.description: openai_chat and openai_responses adapters detect HTTP-end without terminal signal and inject a typed AlephError::Timeout. Gemini adapter silently returns None — a mid-stream EOF surfaces as a normal EndTurn.
findings.fix: Mirror anthropic/adapter.rs::queue_has_terminal + stream_was_truncated pattern: reuse delta::has_terminal_delta, push Timeout when no terminal signal seen.

findings.title: extract_codex_account_id parses JWT on every Codex request
findings.description: build_request calls extract_codex_account_id(api_key) per turn: split('.') + base64-decode payload + serde_json::from_slice + field walk. account_id is stable for the token's lifetime.
findings.fix: Cache (key -> account_id) on OpenAiResponsesProtocol via OnceCell/RwLock, or hoist account_id onto CodexAuth as a derived field populated in OAuthTokenCache::from_auth.

findings.title: AlephError::config used for 136+ DB errors with misleading TOML suggestion
findings.description: Hardcoded suggestion reads 'Check your configuration file at ~/.aleph/config.toml' but the actual error is a DB connection / FK / serialization failure. memory_events.rs uses AlephError::other (no misleading suggestion) — proving the inconsistency.

findings.title: memories table + vec0 + FTS5 + triggers dead in state.db
findings.description: Real memory storage is in memory.db via memory/store/sqlite/. Resilience state.db has duplicate dead schema including memories_vec (vec0 1024-dim), memories_fts, 2 sync triggers, 3 indexes. Triggers never fire (no inserts).

findings.title: 7 tables duplicated from memory.db (compression_sessions / graph_* / daily_insights / dream_status)
findings.description: compression_sessions, graph_nodes, graph_edges, graph_aliases, memory_entities, daily_insights, dream_status are created in state.db but only ever read/written in memory.db (different file, different backend).

findings.title: Shadow Replay recovery fields (checkpoint_snapshot_path, last_tool_call_id) unused
findings.description: Both fields written by insert_agent_task but never read by any recovery code path. Real recovery uses reconcile_orphaned_tasks which ignores them.

findings.title: Recursive Sentry fields (recursion_depth, parent_task_id, with_parent_task) are aspirational
findings.description: Schema columns + struct fields + builder method exist but no code enforces, increments, or reads them. AgentTask::new always sets recursion_depth=0, parent_task_id=None.

findings.title: should_auto_resume and needs_resume_confirmation unused
findings.description: Both AgentTask recovery-decision methods defined + tested but never called in production. Actual recovery is unconditional Running->Interrupted via reconcile_orphaned_tasks.

findings.title: TaskStatus::Idle and ::Swapped never produced (only round-trip)
findings.description: Two of seven TaskStatus variants are documented as Session-as-a-Service but no production path writes them. Accept via from_str_or_default, never written by reconcile or update_task_status.

findings.title: identity_links only on configured-bindings path
findings.description: Zero-config fallback (resolve_session_key_with_agent) ignores identity_links; only the configured-bindings path consults them. Documented but still a real gap.

findings.title: OutcomeObserver reacts only to SessionCompleted
findings.description: All non-SessionCompleted events are forwarded but produce no routing record; absence of 'recording' logs is indistinguishable from empty-result paths.

findings.title: OnceLock::set result discarded silently on second recall
findings.description: build_routing_experience_message uses let _ = attribution.task_emb.set(task_emb.clone()); a second recall silently loses its embedding, breaking D6 record/recall symmetry.

findings.title: Main key parser silently re-types main_key=peer|dm|ephemeral
findings.description: parse_rest excludes peer|dm|ephemeral from the [main_key] arm; a Main key with such a main_key will not round-trip. project_room does not validate against this reservation.

findings.title: SessionKey::task panics on reserved task_type
findings.description: Library panic on a String input; no Result, no shared is_reserved_task_type helper, docstring says 'must not be' but does not warn of panic.

findings.title: runtime_error format makes the stderr tail uncatchable at the gateway boundary
findings.description: AlephError::runtime() output embeds the stderr tail as 'Stderr tail: <X>\n\nFix options: ...'. The gateway handler at src/gateway/handlers/runtimes.rs:175 recovers the tail via err_str.split_once("Stderr tail: ").map(|(_, tail)| tail.to_string()) which captures everything AFTER the marker — including the Fix options block. The 'stderr' field of RuntimeInstallProgressEvent therefore carries noise in addition to the actual stderr.
findings.fix: Stop encoding stderr in the human-readable error message; expose it as a structured field on AlephError::runtime or a new variant, and have runtime_error return a struct the gateway can serialize field-by-field.

findings.title: CapabilityEntry::source and last_probed are dead data
findings.description: source and last_probed are written by every code path (ensure.rs, runtime_warmup.rs, gateway/handlers/runtimes.rs::handle_refresh, migrate_from_legacy, tests) but never read. CapabilitySource::AlephManaged vs System has no observable effect. last_probed is referenced in the doc-comment for revalidate_ready ('the recorded version stays as-of last_probed, which is why that field exists') but no code consults it for re-probe scheduling. CapabilityStatus::Stale is similarly written only by migrate_from_legacy and never set by the live codepath.
findings.fix: Delete the fields and the Stale variant if nothing is planned to use them, or wire them into the re-probe scheduler so the existing infrastructure pays for itself.

findings.title: Stage lists live in mod.rs::from_strategy, not strategy.rs
findings.description: strategy.rs is 58 lines of mostly re-exports; the per-strategy stage lists are in dreaming/mod.rs::from_strategy (a ~100-line vec![Box::new(...)] block). Moving the lists into strategy.rs would shorten from_strategy and make the three strategies diffable.
findings.fix: Add impl DreamStrategy { fn stage_list(&self, cfg, policy) -> Vec<Box<dyn DreamStage>> } in strategy.rs and have from_strategy call through. Mechanical, low risk.

findings.title: pending field docstring claims a background flush task that does not exist
findings.description: The docstring says 'the background flush task drains in batches via flush_pending (wired in B5.2)'. No tokio::spawn exists, no task handle field, no test for flush-without-push. The B5.2 marker at agent_init/mod.rs:185-186 is a different concern (hoisting the manager out of local scope).
findings.fix: Either implement the background task the docstring promises, or rewrite the docstring to describe the actual producer/consumer. Downstream of F-02.

findings.title: Static Regex::new(...).unwrap() repeated across 5 sites with disable-next-line comment
findings.description: LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(...).unwrap()) appears in helpers.rs, wikilink.rs, supersession.rs, ingest/apply.rs. The unwrap is only a panic risk if the pattern itself is malformed. A small helper would eliminate the repeated unwrap.
findings.fix: Introduce a static_regex! macro or a regex() helper at the crate root.

findings.title: TODO marker for partial-rendering optimization in refresh_index_after_ingest
findings.description: Doc comment 'TODO (Phase B follow-up)' describing an unfinished optimization (full rebuild instead of category-scoped render). Already documented as deferred; flagging only so the stale-TODO filter does not drop it.
findings.fix: Implement the partial rendering or schedule for a named issue.

findings.title: 25 default-implemented stub methods on NoteStore trait mask mock fidelity
findings.description: The NoteStore trait has 25+ default methods returning Ok(()) / Ok(Vec::new()) for non-SQLite backends and test mocks, each with let _ = (param1, param2, ...); stubs. Any signature change is invisible to mocks.
findings.fix: Either consolidate the stubs behind a MockNoteStore blank impl, or split into a small required-methods core + optional-extension trait. Note for follow-up.

findings.title: strip_md_ext silently passes .md-suffixed titles through
findings.description: strip_md_ext is the filename chokepoint. With the new policy rejecting '..', a title carrying .md is allowed through sanitize_title and stripped here. The behaviour is correct for current callers; flagging as fragile to a future refactor that splits filename and title concerns.
findings.fix: N/A in current code.

findings.title: Watcher overuses Vec::new() as 'reconcile every corpus' sentinel
findings.description: The producer and consumer agree that paths.is_empty() means 'reconcile every corpus' (MAX_PATHS_PER_BATCH gate). The producer currently uses md_count before sort/dedup to gate this so empty-after-filter cannot reach the bulk branch, but the meaning of 'empty Vec' is overloaded: deliberate bulk vs. all events filtered.
findings.fix: Use an enum WatcherMsg { Bulk, Paths(Vec<PathBuf>) } instead of overloading the empty Vec.

findings.title: Watcher canonicalize().unwrap_or(root) silently keeps un-canonicalized root on failure
findings.description: On canonicalize failure (permission denied, missing path), the code keeps the un-resolved root without logging. On platforms where notify reports the un-resolved path, this produces a silently-broken watcher that filters every event as 'not a note'.
findings.fix: Log a warn! on the unwrap_or branch so operators can diagnose a running-but-empty watcher.

findings.title: RippleTask default shape not explicitly tested
findings.description: RippleConfig has an explicit test; RippleTask (task.rs) does not. Field-level reader-vs-writer coverage is plausibly complete (one quick scan) but the test gap is real. Worth a follow-up grep-diff pass.
findings.fix: Add a one-line test for RippleTask::default() shape, mirroring the existing RippleConfig test.

findings.title: #[allow(dead_code)] on test-only accessor is unnecessary
findings.description: conn() is pub(crate), cfg(test), but the #[allow(dead_code)] annotation is present even though the function has callers in the test module (sqlite/notes/tests.rs:153).
findings.fix: Drop the #[allow(dead_code)] annotation.

findings.title: raw_where helper is load-bearing for the count/list agreement invariant
findings.description: The 'phantom-page bug' review required count_raw_memories and get_raw_memories_dashboard to share a WHERE clause via the raw_where helper. The helper is now load-bearing for every raw-memories filter; this is FYI, not a bug.
findings.fix: Make raw_where pub(crate) and add a doc comment instructing any new SELECT against raw_memories to build its WHERE through the helper.

findings.title: hybrid_search_notes runs vector_search then search_notes_fts serially under one Mutex<Connection>
findings.description: KNN and FTS5 halves of a hybrid query cannot overlap because both hold the connection mutex. Not a correctness bug; a missed concurrency opportunity. Cannot fix without a connection pool.
findings.fix: N/A — out of audit scope.

findings.title: Drop warning branch suppresses the debug log for slow operations (acknowledged deferred design)
findings.description: When target_ms > 0, enable_warnings = true, and elapsed_ms > threshold_ms, Drop emits tracing::warn! and returns, bypassing the tracing::debug! that would otherwise carry the structured timing record (duration_ms, metadata, stage). Slow operations leave no structured debug trail. Deferred to design-level decision per commit 1f90366f4.
findings.fix: No action unless revisiting the deferred item. If revisited, drop the early `return;` so both warn and debug fire for slow operations.

findings.title: Inconsistent re-init log level vs defaults_override::init_defaults_override
findings.description: Both init_metrics_runtime and defaults_override::init_defaults_override implement write-once OnceLock::set semantics with silently-discarded re-inits. They diverge on log level: metrics uses tracing::debug! while defaults_override uses warn!. Same 'lost write' failure mode, different visibility. The defaults_override variant explicitly states the operational consequence ('silently inactive — restart the process'), which the metrics variant hides at DEBUG.
findings.fix: Promote to tracing::warn! with the same actionable phrasing, or extract a shared init_once! macro so both call sites cannot drift.

findings.title: Drop warning branch and init_metrics_runtime / MetricsRuntime have no behavioral tests
findings.description: Twelve in-module tests cover only builder field state and elapsed_ms bounds. The Drop tracing::warn!/debug! emissions, the init_metrics_runtime is_finite() guard, the MetricsRuntime::warning_threshold_ms arithmetic, the MetricsRuntime::default values, and the OnceLock set-conflict path all lack behavioral coverage. Two test names (test_timer_drop_logs, test_timer_target_zero_no_warning) imply behavior the tests do not verify — a maintenance hazard.
findings.fix: Add tests with tracing-subscriber's TestWriter (or tracing-test) to capture emitted events across the (target_ms > 0, threshold_exceeded, enable_warnings) × (enable_logging) × (target_ms = 0) matrix. Add table-driven unit tests for warning_threshold_ms covering target_ms = 0, target_ms = u64::MAX, multiplier = 0.0.

findings.title: DEFAULT_WARNING_MULTIPLIER is duplicated independently of MetricsPolicy::default_warning_multiplier
findings.description: The value 2.0 is independently encoded in three places: DEFAULT_WARNING_MULTIPLIER const (mod.rs:28), default_warning_multiplier() const fn (config/types/policies/metrics.rs:53-55), and the serde default attribute (config/types/policies/metrics.rs:43). If the policy default ever changes, the runtime fallback would still use the old value silently — any pre-init StageTimer (test, early startup) would see a different threshold than configured.
findings.fix: Source both defaults from one location — either pub const in config::types::policies::metrics consumed by metrics::DEFAULT_WARNING_MULTIPLIER, or expose MetricsPolicy::DEFAULT_WARNING_MULTIPLIER and have MetricsRuntime::default read it.

findings.title: Module doc overstates capabilities; 'detailed instrumentation when enabled' is not a real mode
findings.description: Module doc claims the module is 'designed to have minimal overhead when profiling is disabled and detailed instrumentation when enabled.' The actual API has only two binary toggles (enable_logging, enable_warnings); the debug branch emits exactly the same fields whether enable_logging is on or off — it only gates whether the record is emitted at all. The phrase implies a richer profiling mode that doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Trim the sentence to: 'It is designed to have minimal overhead when logging is disabled (enable_logging = false) and to emit a debug-level record per stage when enabled.'

findings.title: MetricsRuntime::warning_threshold_ms is pub but MetricsRuntime itself is private — the pub is no-op
findings.description: MetricsRuntime is a private struct (no pub). metrics_runtime() returns MetricsRuntime by Copy so module-internal code can call warning_threshold_ms, but external crates cannot name the type. The pub keyword and #[must_use] on warning_threshold_ms are inert — they expand public API surface that nobody can reach. The #[must_use] on a u64-returning method is also a code smell that forces _ = or let _ = on every discard.
findings.fix: Drop pub (and the #[must_use]) on warning_threshold_ms since MetricsRuntime is module-private. Alternatively, expose MetricsRuntime deliberately as part of the public API.

findings.title: Orchestrator::new takes 6 Arc params positionally; HarnessRunner has 7 separate capability getters
findings.description: Implicit builder with positional Arc<dyn Trait> args — easy to mis-order at call site (would compile, route wrong service). HarnessRunner trait has 7 capability getters each with a default None; no compile-time enforcement of which ones production gateways must set.

findings.title: Orchestrator fields are all pub; no compile-time enforcement of builders
findings.description: All 9 fields are pub, including active_sessions: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>. with_subagent_routing/with_agent_registry function as documentation only. Direct field writes possible after construction; race risk on the lock guard itself.

findings.title: memory_injection_headroom does full session log read on hot path
findings.description: get_events(session_id, None, None) called every run for token arithmetic. context_pressure_reminder repeats it. Harness also reads events in runner_impl.rs:1169-1170. Three full scans per turn for a long-lived session.

findings.title: load_prompt_extra_files reads files synchronously with no initial size cap
findings.description: std::fs::read_to_string on every path in [prompt.extra_files] with no upper bound on read. Window-scaled per-file cap is applied AFTER full read. A multi-GB file at a configured path blocks the executor on every turn.

findings.title: load_user_flows_from_dir aborts entire load on first malformed TOML
findings.description: Single bad file prevents ALL other user flows from loading. No per-file WARN, no continuation past recoverable errors. Symptom: 'my custom flows disappeared' with no diagnostic.

findings.title: SessionResolution::is_new is computed but never read in production
findings.description: is_new computed on every resolve_session call; only test files assert on it. No production consumer. Doubly redundant with seed_history's own 'log already non-empty' probe.

findings.title: init and reload build different lookup tables (duplicated code)
findings.description: PiiEngine::new and PiiEngine::reload both rebuild custom_rule_actions and excluded_providers, but the constructions are open-coded in two places (not extracted into a helper). If a future field is added (e.g. effective_providers or a fast-path phone_digit_set), the same code must be edited in three places (new, reload, and the effective_config indexing path). Drift is a likely failure mode.
findings.fix: Extract fn lookup_tables(config: &PrivacyConfig) -> (HashMap<String, PiiAction>, HashSet<String>) and call it from both new and reload.

findings.title: effective_config clones PrivacyConfig on three early-return paths
findings.description: effective_config has three early-return branches — no platform, no platform policy, policy with all-None fields — each returning self.config.clone(). With pii_filtering: true, seven PiiAction defaults, and a few Vecs/HashMaps in PrivacyConfig, each clone is a one-shot allocation per filter call. Hot path, easily avoidable.
findings.fix: Return a thin enum (e.g. EffectiveConfig<'a> { Global(&'a PrivacyConfig), Owned(PrivacyConfig) }) and match in filter_with_config, or split into effective_config_owned and a borrowing version for the identity cases.

findings.title: Bearer-token char class misses +/= (base64 padding)
findings.description: The Bearer branch (?i:Bearer)\s+[a-zA-Z0-9._\-]{20,} accepts alphanumerics plus ., _, -. Standard base64 alphabet also includes +, /, =. A Bearer <token> containing those characters is not matched by ApiKeyRule. runtime_guard's ExecLeakDetector covers this with a broader bearer_token rule (per src/exec/leak_detector.rs:239-260), but the PII module's stand-alone capability is documented as filters-outbound — a leaky Bearer in a context where only the PII module ran would slip through.
findings.fix: Widen the bearer token char class to [a-zA-Z0-9._\-+/=]{20,} or add an explicit \+ branch. Add a regression test asserting that Bearer abc+def/ghi= is detected by the PII rule alone.

findings.title: UnifiedMessage::from_provider_response only used in tests
findings.description: Reverse ProviderResponse -> UnifiedMessage constructor has zero production callers. Session history persistence paths use delta::*replay_* helpers directly. Pub exposure makes accidental external dependency risk.
findings.fix: Annotate #[allow(dead_code)] with documented expected caller, or delete.

findings.title: queue_has_terminal duplicates delta::has_terminal_delta
findings.description: Two byte-identical functions: delta::has_terminal_delta (pub(crate)) used by openai_chat/responses, and anthropic/adapter.rs::queue_has_terminal (private) used only by anthropic. Both have separate test coverage of the same logic.
findings.fix: Delete anthropic's local queue_has_terminal, import and call delta::has_terminal_delta for consistency. Keep stream_was_truncated (composes two flags, slightly different semantics).

findings.title: ProviderRegistry::names() returns Vec<String> with per-call allocation
findings.description: Hot-query structure (read on every route_status RPC). Each call: sort + clone every String key. Unnecessary Vec<String> allocation when Vec<&str> borrowed from HashMap keys suffices.
findings.fix: Change return type to Vec<&str> and borrow from self.providers.keys().

findings.title: retry.rs contains only apply_jitter after cleanup
findings.description: Module-level doc is review-residue history ('what was deleted and why'). With only one live function (apply_jitter), the file's identity doesn't match its name.
findings.fix: Rename file to jitter.rs, or migrate apply_jitter into llm_retry.rs to consolidate retry-related utilities.

findings.title: reconcile_orphaned_tasks returns pre-update snapshot (status stale)
findings.description: Returned AgentTask Vec has status=Running (snapshot) while DB has status=Interrupted. Current callers don't read task.status, so harmless today; footgun for future callers.

findings.title: 3 of 7 agent_tasks CRUD methods unused outside tests
findings.description: get_tasks_by_session, get_recoverable_tasks, mark_running_as_interrupted have no production callers. The latter two are only invoked internally by reconcile_orphaned_tasks and by tests.

findings.title: mark_running_as_interrupted doesn't set completed_at (state-machine inconsistency)
findings.description: update_task_status sets completed_at for Completed/Failed. The bulk path Running->Interrupted leaves completed_at NULL, indistinguishable from 'started but never finished'. Combines poorly with finding R-L3.

findings.title: 7 of 11 trace methods unused outside tests
findings.description: bulk_insert_traces, get_last_trace, get_traces_from_step, delete_traces_for_task, get_trace_count, list_trace_tasks, get_trace_by_id. Built for Shadow Replay resume which never materialized.

findings.title: Module name promises reconnect/retry/backoff that does not exist
findings.description: Per grep: src/resilience/ contains zero retry/backoff/reconnect/circuit-breaker code. Module is purely persistence + types. Audit brief's expectation comes from aspirational doc comments in types.rs.

findings.title: context_tokens/context_window hardcoded to 0
findings.description: Two schema columns are always written as 0; a future renderer will treat zero as real measurement. Documented but still worst-of-both-worlds.

findings.title: Vault-only provider mishandled as Unknown
findings.description: A provider reachable only via vault (no config entry) is rendered as Unknown, which fail-opens the recall block tag. The LLM picks it up and only discovers the misfire on first call.

findings.title: agent_id verbatim vs session_key normalised split
findings.description: ResolvedRoute.agent_id is the raw config string while session_key uses normalized form; intentional but the contract is comment-only and easy to misread.

findings.title: format_dm_base PerPeer empty-channel branch is legacy-only
findings.description: The empty-channel PerPeer arm is only reachable through SessionKey::peer (legacy alias); refactoring that removes the alias silently makes the arm unreachable.

findings.title: enrich_path_for_reprobe mutates process-wide PATH
findings.description: The function permanently mutates the daemon's PATH via std::env::set_var("PATH", joined). PATH_LOCK makes the read-modify-write atomic against other prepend_existing_dirs callers, but does not prevent other modules from reading PATH concurrently. Tokio's set_var is unsafe in Rust 2024+; under edition 2021 it carries the documented 'not thread-safe' warning. The risk window is microseconds, so this is a latent risk rather than a current defect.
findings.fix: Switch the daemon to a single Arc<Mutex<OsString>> PATH-equivalent and pass it explicitly to Command::env("PATH", ...), mirroring what probe.rs::enriched_search_path already does correctly.

findings.title: CapabilityStatus::Bootstrapping has no transition guard
findings.description: The state machine records Bootstrapping in the ledger at line 173, then immediately transitions out. No code path reads the Bootstrapping value to gate behavior. In gateway/handlers/runtimes.rs::handle_refresh there is no check for Bootstrapping; a refresh arriving while ensure_capability holds its install guard can write Missing (probe-failed) over a ledger entry that is mid-install. The bootstrap's eventual Ready write repairs the state, but the variant + field are essentially documentation-in-the-type-system.
findings.fix: Either drop the variant (it is not used as a state) or wire it into handle_refresh to skip entries that are currently Bootstrapping.

findings.title: Nested lock acquisition order in ensure_capability_recursive has no global invariant
findings.description: The function acquires the outer capability's lock BEFORE recursing into each dependency (capability_lock(cap) -> .lock().await -> for dep in deps { recurse(dep) }). capability_lock(name) returns Arc<Mutex<()>> keyed by name, with no per-spec ordering rule. Current SPECS are safe (only node -> fnm, playwright-cli -> node). But the data-driven shape of SPECS means any future addition that lists deps in conflicting orders would deadlock without MAX_BOOTSTRAP_DEPTH catching it.
findings.fix: Either enforce a global lock order (sort deps by name before acquiring) or document explicitly in RuntimeSpec.deps that lock ordering is by name.

findings.title: fnm list parsing is fragile against future fnm output formats
findings.description: The parser hard-codes two assumptions: the default version line begins with '*' and a version token in that line begins with 'v'. Recent fnm releases have changed column delimiters; if the default line no longer starts with '*', every node install produces NoNodeVersion and the 'lts' alias is silently never created.
findings.fix: Prefer 'fnm current' (which returns just the current default version, no parsing) over scanning 'fnm list'.

findings.title: find_on_path and get_version have no timeout
findings.description: probe::probe runs 'which'/'where' and '<bin> --version' with no timeout wrapper. The bootstrap path (bootstrap.rs::run_cmd) wraps its child in timeout(Duration::from_secs(600), ...); the probe does not. A binary on PATH that hangs on --version (a script without signal handling, a GUI binary that prompts, a fnm install under a corrupted network mount) will hang the probe indefinitely, blocking daemon startup warmup and every subsequent ensure_capability that hits the same name.
findings.fix: Wrap the which/where/--version invocations in tokio::time::timeout (and convert probe::probe to async fn to match the rest of the orchestrator), with a fallback None on timeout.
